fichas.title: Pergolas and trellises: design and construction
fichas.summary: Pergolas form outdoor spaces with rows of columns or pillars and may lead to viewpoints, divide spaces, or provide sitting areas. Their position and function should be considered, and overhead construction is generally lighter than the vertical supports. Timber uprights should be protected from ground damp. Trellises support climbing plants and can serve as visual barriers. The illustrated details show post fixings, timber and masonry supports, and a steel pergola.
uses: Lead to viewpoints or special places

fichas.title: Espalier and cordon training layouts
fichas.summary: Illustrated layouts show vertical cordon, U-shaped cordon, palmette verrier, and chandelier palmette training. The page also depicts timber supports for espalier-trained fruit trees and a wall-fixed trellis. Support spacing and growth height should be selected for the intended plants and local conditions.
uses: Arrange plant growth in linear or full-area patterns

fichas.title: Climbing and winding plants: selection and heights
fichas.summary: The page provides height ranges for annual climbing plants and a reference table of perennial climbing and winding species, including growth rate, trellis need, seasonal leaves, watering, flowering, and location. Plant selection and support spacing should account for growth height and local conditions. Location symbols distinguish sunny, semi-shaded, and shaded positions.
uses: Select climbing plants for pergolas and trellises
